description.en-US: Personal patchwork builds of ScreenTime, RecurringExpenseTracker and Fcitx5 for Android.

summary.en-US: Easily track the time you spend on your device and apps.

description.en-US:
Screen Time is a simple app that lets you easily track the time you spend on your device and apps.

Features:

- Displays total screen time for your device over the past week or for a chosen day.
- Comparative graph showing screen time across different days of the week.
- Comparative graph displaying screen time for each hour of the day.
- Ability to view screen time and comparative graphs for each individual app.
- Comparative list of screen time for each app, sorted from the most used to the least used during the chosen period.
- Simple and modern interface.
- Home screen widget.
- No ads.
- No data collection (internet permissions disabled).
- Open source.
- Developed in Kotlin with Jetpack Compose and Material 3.

The source code is available here: https://gitlab.com/Atharok/ScreenTime

summary.en-US: Keep track of your monthly spending

description.en-US:
A Material You recurring expense tracker, allowing you to keep track of your monthly spending.

As the name suggests, this app focuses on recurring expenses like rent, insurance, subscriptions, and other regular payments.
Built with Kotlin Multiplatform and Material You design principles, it provides a simple yet powerful way to track and visualize your recurring financial commitments.
The app is designed to be intuitive and straightforward, helping you understand exactly where your money goes each month.
My idea is to add new features iteratively, and I'm happy for any contribution. Feel free to make feature requests or report bugs if you find any.

summary.en-US: Fcitx5 input method framework and engines, with Rime sync fixes

description.en-US:
Fcitx5 for Android is the Android port of the Fcitx5 input method framework.
It ships Pinyin (with Shuangpin support), Wubi and table-based input methods and
can be extended with plugins such as Rime, Anthy, Hangul, Chewing, UniKey,
Sayura, Thai and Jyutping.

This patchwork build starts from upstream 0.1.3 and adds:
- the "All files access" (MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE) permission, so librime
can write its sync_dir on shared storage (for example Download/Rime-Sync);
- a built-in Rime/Fcitx5 configuration file manager and UTF-8 editor;
- cleanup of stale .temp.userdb files at startup, avoiding LOCK conflicts
during sync;
- a horizontal back arrow in the file manager.

Note: the package name matches the official app but the signing key differs,
so the official version must be uninstalled before installing this build.

Fcitx5 for Android is free software under the LGPL-2.1; the corresponding
source is the upstream repository plus the patch queue in this repository.
